title: Car Shipping in Babylon, NY | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: Car shipping from Babylon, NY and the Town of Babylon. Open and enclosed carriers, door-to-door, snowbird and relocation moves. Call (631) 430-6725 to book.
heroSub: Door-to-door auto transport from the Village of Babylon, West Babylon, Lindenhurst, Copiague, Deer Park and the rest of the Town of Babylon. Open or enclosed, FMCSA-licensed, with a local office on West Main Street.
intro:
Car shipping from Babylon, NY works a little differently than it does up on the North Shore or out in Nassau. The south shore of Suffolk County is built around the water: canals in the village and Lindenhurst, dead-end streets that stop at a bulkhead, and parkways that were never meant for a 75-foot car hauler. Our office at 57 W Main St #306, a short walk from the Babylon LIRR station, books open and enclosed transport for the Village of Babylon and the whole Town of Babylon, from Amityville on the Nassau line to West Islip and the Bay Shore border.

Most of the cars we move out of here fall into a few buckets: snowbirds heading to Florida for the winter, families and tradespeople relocating off Long Island for good, and boaters or second-home owners who want a vehicle moved before or after the season. Whatever the reason, Babylon auto transport comes down to the same two questions: where can the truck safely get to, and when do you need the car on the other end. Call (631) 430-6725 and we will answer both.

sections.h2: Getting a car hauler into the Town of Babylon
sections.html:
The Southern State Parkway runs right through North Babylon and Deer Park, but commercial trucks are banned on it, and its stone overpasses are low enough that a loaded hauler would not clear them anyway. That shapes every pickup we schedule here. Carriers coming from the west stay on the Long Island Expressway to Exit 51 or 52 and come south on Route 231 (Deer Park Avenue) or Commack Road, or they drop down to Sunrise Highway (NY-27) and work their way in from there. From the east it is Sunrise Highway almost every time, with Route 109 and Route 110 as the north-south connectors into West Babylon and Lindenhurst.

Montauk Highway (NY-27A) is the only through road in the village that can handle a full-size carrier, and even that gets tight at the Main Street shops on a Saturday. Drivers usually prefer to stage on Sunrise Highway near the Great East Neck Road or Route 109 interchanges, then run a single car in with a smaller truck or ask you to meet them nearby. If a dispatcher tells you the truck will come down the Southern State, that is a sign they do not know Long Island. Ours do.

sections.h2: Meeting points when your block will not take a truck
sections.html:
Half the streets south of Montauk Highway end at the water. The canal blocks off Fire Island Avenue in the village, Venetian Shores in Lindenhurst and the Great Neck Road canals in Copiague are narrow, tree-lined and finish in a cul-de-sac with no room to turn a tractor-trailer around.

For those addresses we set a meeting point when the order is booked, not the morning of pickup. The usual choices:

  • Babylon LIRR station lot on Railroad Avenue, the end of the electrified Babylon branch. Big, flat and easy to find for a driver who has never been to the village.
  • Sunrise Highway shopping plazas in West Babylon and Lindenhurst, where the loading lanes are built for tractor-trailers.
  • Route 231 near the Sunrise Highway interchange for North Babylon and Deer Park customers.
  • The Republic Airport area in East Farmingdale for Wyandanch and Wheatley Heights pickups, since Route 110 is wide open there.

sections.h2: Snowbird car shipping from Babylon to Florida
sections.html:
The Town of Babylon sends a steady stream of retirees south every fall, and a lot of them have been splitting the year between the south shore and Florida for decades. The Gulf side is the heavy favorite from here: Naples, Fort Myers, Sarasota, Bradenton and the Tampa area. On the Atlantic side we run plenty of cars to Boca Raton, Delray Beach, West Palm Beach, Jupiter and down into Broward.

Typical open-carrier pricing from Babylon to Florida for a running sedan sits around $650 to $750 with two to four days in transit, but the calendar matters more than the mileage. Late October through mid-December is peak southbound, and the week after Thanksgiving is the single busiest stretch of the year. Book two to three weeks ahead for those dates. Coming home, April and early May are crowded northbound, so if you are flexible, leaving Florida in late March or waiting until mid-May gets you a better rate and a faster pickup.

sections.h2: Pickups and work vans leaving Long Island for good
sections.html:
Babylon is a trades town. Plumbers, electricians, landscapers, HVAC techs and contractors have been the backbone of West Babylon, Lindenhurst, Copiague and Deer Park for generations, and lately a lot of them are relocating to the Carolinas, Tennessee and Florida, where the cost of living and the property taxes look very different from Suffolk County. When they go, they are usually taking a pickup, a work van or both.

Shipping a work vehicle is not the same as shipping a sedan. A Ford F-250 or Ram 2500 with a lift, a ladder rack or a utility body is taller and heavier than a standard car-hauler slot, and a Transit or Sprinter high-roof van will not fit on most open carriers at all without a top-deck position. Tell us the exact configuration up front, including rack height, and we will quote it right the first time. Expect a modest surcharge for oversized trucks, and plan on an empty bed and cab; carriers cannot legally haul tools and household goods inside the vehicle.

sections.h2: Great South Bay salt air, flood zones and the enclosed question
sections.html:
If your car lives south of Montauk Highway, it lives in salt air. For a daily driver, open transport is the right call: cheaper, more trucks, and a few days on the highway will not change anything.

Enclosed transport makes sense here in two situations. The first is anything you care about keeping pristine: a classic, a low-mileage sports car, a restored truck. Enclosed runs roughly 40 to 60 percent more than open from this area and the trucks are fewer, so give us an extra week of lead time. The second is timing around weather. Large parts of the Village of Babylon, Lindenhurst, Copiague and West Islip sit in FEMA flood zones, and plenty of people here lost vehicles to saltwater in Sandy. We regularly get calls to move a second car inland or down to a relative's place in Florida ahead of a forecast storm. An open carrier will do that job fine; the point is to book early, because once a hurricane watch is posted every carrier on Long Island is suddenly full.

sections.h2: Boats, Fire Island and the summer calendar
sections.html:
From Memorial Day through Labor Day, the Robert Moses Causeway and Montauk Highway through the village are jammed with beach traffic to Robert Moses State Park and Captree, and the Fire Island ferry lots in Bay Shore fill by mid-morning. Carriers know this and tend to schedule Babylon pickups early in the morning or after 7 p.m. in summer. If you have a weekday morning window, say so when you book.

Summer is also when boaters and second-home owners move cars. We ship vehicles for people who keep a boat at the Babylon or Lindenhurst marinas but live out of state, and for Long Islanders who want a second car at their place in Florida or the Carolinas without the drive. If you are renting on the barrier beaches for the summer, we can time delivery to your lease dates.

faqs.q: Can a car carrier get down my canal street in Babylon Village or Lindenhurst?
faqs.a: Usually not. The canal blocks off Fire Island Avenue, in Venetian Shores and along the Copiague canals are too narrow for a full-size hauler to turn around. We will set a nearby meeting spot when you book, most often the Babylon LIRR lot on Railroad Avenue or a Sunrise Highway plaza. Some carriers run a smaller flatbed for the last mile, which we can request if you prefer true door service.

faqs.q: Why won't the driver just take the Southern State to my house in North Babylon?
faqs.a: Commercial trucks are prohibited on the Southern State Parkway, and the stone overpasses are too low for a loaded car hauler regardless. Carriers reach North Babylon and Deer Park from the Long Island Expressway via Route 231 (Deer Park Avenue) or Commack Road, or from Sunrise Highway heading north. That adds a few minutes, but it is the only legal way in, and a dispatcher who says otherwise does not know the route.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book a snowbird car to Florida from Babylon?
faqs.a: Two to three weeks for pickup dates between late October and mid-December, and the same for the April return. Outside of those windows a week is usually enough. Open transport from Babylon to Naples, Fort Myers or West Palm Beach runs about $650 to $750 for a sedan, two to four days in transit. Enclosed is available but there are fewer trucks, so add a few days of lead time.

faqs.q: Can you ship my work van or lifted pickup when I move to the Carolinas?
faqs.a: Yes. We move F-250s, Ram 2500s, Transits and Sprinters out of West Babylon and Deer Park every month. High-roof vans and lifted trucks need a specific slot on the carrier, so give us the height, rack details and whether the vehicle runs. Expect a surcharge of roughly $100 to $250 over a standard vehicle. The bed and cab must be empty; carriers cannot transport tools or household goods.

faqs.q: I'm in a flood zone near the Great South Bay. Can you move my car before a storm?
faqs.a: We can, if you call early. Once a hurricane or nor'easter watch is posted for Long Island, carriers fill up within a day. Call (631) 430-6725 as soon as the forecast looks serious and we will try to get a truck in through Sunrise Highway or the LIE within 24 to 48 hours. Sending the car to family inland or to a Florida address both work, and open carriers are fine for this.
